name: Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah
role: Emir of Kuwait (since 2023); previously crown prince and security official
summary: Mishal has prioritized executive authority, security and action against corruption, suspending the elected parliament and some constitutional provisions in 2024. His public speeches also endorse environmental measures, collective Gulf security and Kuwait’s right to self-defense.

sources.title: Address dissolving the National Assembly (10 May 2024), full translated text
sources.author: Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah, reproduced by Times Kuwait
sources.usedFor: Parliament, executive powers, corruption, security and citizenship.

sources.title: Will Kuwait’s Parliamentary Democracy Be Restored, Reformed, or Repudiated? (13 March 2025)
sources.author: Omar Al Jasser and Nathan J. Brown, Carnegie Endowment
sources.usedFor: Emir’s suspension decree, crown-prince appointment and citizenship changes.

sources.title: BTI 2026 Country Report: Kuwait

sources.title: Middle East Green Initiative summit speech (25 October 2021), reported extracts
sources.author: Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah, reported by Kuwait Times
sources.usedFor: Personal endorsement of emission reductions, reserves, renewable energy and future-generation sustainability.

sources.title: Ramadan address, full text, Times Kuwait 15–21 March 2026, pp. 3 and 5
sources.author: Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah
sources.usedFor: Self-defense under the UN Charter, collective Gulf security, armed forces and remembrance of martyrs.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: He suspended the legislature and assumed its powers rather than requiring an elected parliament’s continuing authorization.

close-ties-china.rationale: His China visit and cooperation agreements establish engagement, but not a stated preference for relying on China rather than the United States.

collective-defense.rationale: His 2026 speech called Gulf security indivisible and treated an attack on a sister state as a threat to all.

democracy-best.rationale: He defended suspending elected parliamentary government when he judged its conduct harmful, making democracy conditional on state interests.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He endorsed emission reduction, new reserves, oil-sector rehabilitation, efficiency and renewable energy as government measures against climate change.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: His 2024 decision suspended constitutional constraints for up to four years in response to what he described as a grave national crisis.

future-generations.rationale: His environmental speech expressly endorsed sustainable energy supplies for future generations and protection of biodiversity.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on who chooses ministers, and the statement now asks only about command of the armed forces.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: He honored fallen Kuwaiti personnel as righteous martyrs and prayed for their exalted place in the afterlife.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He exercised dynastic monarchical authority and selected another Al Sabah as crown prince without parliamentary vetting.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: He explicitly reserved Kuwait’s right to take necessary military defensive measures against attacks under UN Charter Article 51.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: His speech described widespread corruption reaching government, security, economic and judicial institutions.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: His citizenship amendment added blasphemy among grounds for revoking nationality, authorizing civil punishment for religious speech.

separated-powers.rationale: His suspension transferred parliamentary legislative powers to the emir and cabinet, eliminating the elected legislature’s check.

strong-leader.rationale: He explicitly justified dissolving parliament and suspending constitutional provisions to overcome obstruction and safeguard the country.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: His criticism of fraudulent nationality and improper receipt of benefits does not establish a position on benefits for legally resident immigrants.

women-suffrage.rationale: The parliamentary suspension affected men and women. Neither that act nor general Kuwaiti law establishes his individual view of equal female suffrage.

notes: Research covered his crown-prince speeches, accession, 2024 suspension, later nationality changes and March 2026 address. Full translated 2024 and 2026 speeches were downloaded and read. Targeted searches addressed economy, government, liberty, society/culture, world/globalism, ecology, technology and means. Many economic and social positions remain null because a minister’s proposal, another official’s speech on his behalf, or existing Kuwaiti law is not automatically his position. The parliamentary suspension is described as temporary, not proof he wants to abolish parliament permanently. His earlier public support for democracy is superseded here by the explicit 2024 suspension and justification, while the score does not imply opposition to every consultative arrangement. No living-person inferences or party/royal-family assumptions were used.
